ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the nominal-pi equivalent circuit of a transmission line. In the middle of the upper main line there is a series impedance block, labeled Z; at each end of the series impedance there is a downward shunt branch, both shunt branches are labeled X, and are connected to the bottom common conductor. Reasoning: According to the given Z = 100∠80° Ω, so |Z| = 100 Ω. The reactance magnitude of each shunt branch is X = 3300 Ω, therefore the admittance magnitude of each branch is 1/3300 S. There are two identical shunt branches at the two ends, so the total admittance magnitude |Y| = 1/3300 + 1/3300 = 2/3300 S. The characteristic impedance magnitude is calculated according to |Z0| = sqrt(|Z|/|Y|), namely |Z0| = sqrt(100/(2/3300)) = sqrt(165000) = 406.2 Ω, kept to one decimal place.
